R0270.title: Robot Debug & Maintenance Interface Abuse
R0270.definition: An attack where the attacker abuses exposed robot debug interfaces, maintenance ports, BLE provisioning ports, or vendor-SDK hardcoded credentials to bypass authentication and gain device control or implant backdoors.
R0270.description:
Robot debug & maintenance interface abuse was the most severe embodied-intelligence security incident direction in 2025. The Unitree UniPwn vulnerability series (CVE-2025-35027) affects Go2/G1/H1/B2, originating from a hardcoded AES key in the BLE Wi-Fi provisioning interface (encrypting the string "unitree" bypasses authentication), command injection, allowing attackers to wirelessly gain root with worm-like propagation. CVE-2025-2894 disclosed that Unitree Go1 shipped with the CloudSail remote-access service pre-installed; 1919 devices were once online globally, and anyone with the API key could remotely control devices and access cameras. Alias Robotics' Unitree G1 assessment found FMX dual-layer proprietary encryption used a device-shared static key and telemetry sent to an external IP every 300 seconds. IOActive found in 2017 that Universal Robots UR3/UR5 had missing authentication and could remotely disable the e-stop.

This risk relates to R0166 (IoT default-credentials risk) and R0164 (firmware tampering and backdoors), but is specialized for robot debug/provisioning interfaces and vendor-SDK hardcoded credentials, a severe area for vendor products like Unitree.
R0270.influence: Causes complete robot takeover, firmware tampering, enlistment into botnets, or weaponization as a surveillance node; can spy on users, harm people, or be built into a worm-like robot botnet — UniPwn can auto-infect same-brand robots within Bluetooth range.

observables: Robot BLE provisioning or debug interfaces expose hardcoded credentials that bypass authentication
Devices ship with pre-installed remote-access services exposed to the public internet
Robot firmware is tampered with or backdoored and absorbed into a botnet
Same-brand robots show worm-like auto-propagation within Bluetooth range
Debug interfaces are exploited to gain root and access cameras and actuators
